cases.notes: Sales answers arrive pre-loaded with numbers, which makes this the discipline where a supporting span is easiest to earn and hardest to trust. The dataset carries it as the happy path anyway, because that is what the extractor will meet.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you open a new account?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I rebuilt our discovery script and qualification improved to 60 percent. The questions are shorter and the buyer does most of the talking.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Did that show up in the numbers?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Deals that passed qualification closed in 21 days rather than 45. The ones that did not pass were dropped early instead of lingering.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a hard negotiation.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: In one negotiation I held the discount at 8 percent when the ask was 20. We traded a longer term for it rather than just conceding.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Has anyone else used that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The negotiation playbook I wrote is used by 6 reps. It is two pages and mostly examples that anyone can copy on their next call.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you run your pipeline?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I keep pipeline management tidy every week but I have never counted the hygiene score. It is a habit rather than a metric for me.

evidence.quote_contains: I rebuilt our discovery script and qualification improved to 60 percent
Deals that passed qualification closed in 21 days
In one negotiation I held the discount at 8 percent
The negotiation playbook I wrote is used by 6 reps
I keep pipeline management tidy every week

known_limitations: A stated number makes a span supporting. It does not make the number true: claim verification is a separate concern and this fixture deliberately does not pretend otherwise.

cases.notes: A first year in the seat: one thin example, one honest gap, one topic never reached.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about your discovery process.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I ran discovery on 2 accounts in my first quarter. Both were inbound so the hard part was already done.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: And negotiating?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I am not sure I have a negotiation example at that level. My deals were small enough that price was rarely argued.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How about your pipeline?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: My last role did not really go near that. The territory was handed to me fully built and I never had to prune it.

evidence.quote_contains: I ran discovery on 2 accounts in my first quarter
not sure I have a negotiation example at that level

cases.notes: A genuine conflict about one quota in one year, with pipeline evidence beside it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What was your number?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I carried a quota of 900 thousand last year. It was the first time I had a number that size.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Remind me what was on the plan.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: My quota last year was 1200 thousand. That was the figure on the plan I signed at the start of the year.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you keep the pipeline honest?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: My pipeline management review runs 3 times a week. Anything stale gets closed rather than carried into the following month for no reason.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How much is in it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The pipeline covers 40 open opportunities. Each one has a next step with a date on it, and nothing sits without an owner.

evidence.quote_contains: My pipeline management review runs 3 times a week

contradictions.why: Nine hundred thousand and one thousand two hundred thousand cannot both be last year's quota.

cases.notes: Three words is not an answer to measure. Too little speech is its own state with its own remedy, which is to ask again rather than to score what is there.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a negotiation you led.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: It went fine.
